sections.content:
Looking at the image, the board has rearranged again. Now I see:
- 2 green objects at the top (rows ~3-9)
- Some green objects in the middle area (rows ~25-35)
- Purple objects at top and bottom
- Player at the right side
This is the same rearranged pattern I've seen before. The level keeps rearranging after collecting green objects.
Let me count the green objects and collect them all, being careful about the player's position.
Looking at the image more carefully:
- 2 green objects at top center (rows 3-9)
- 6 green objects in a 2x3 grid on the left (rows 25-35, cols 13-29)
- 3 green objects in a 1x3 row on the right (rows 25-29, cols 37-53)
Total: 11 green objects? That doesn't match the expected 6 remaining.
Wait, the level rearranged when I moved the player. Let me just collect all green objects now.
The player is at the right side. I need to check which green objects are above the player and avoid clicking those first.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Collect all remaining green objects
seg = current_frame.segmentation
nodes = seg['nodes']
player = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'b'][0]
player_cols = [p[1] for p in player['boundary']]
player_min_col = min(player_cols)
player_max_col = max(player_cols)
print(f"Player cols: {player_min_col}-{player_max_col}")

green_objects = [n for n in nodes if n['color'] == 'N']
print(f"Green: {len(green_objects)}")

# Check which are above player
for n in green_objects:
    cols = [p[1] for p in n['boundary']]
    above = min(cols) >= player_min_col - 2 and max(cols) <= player_max_col + 2
    print(f"  cols {min(cols)}-{max(cols)}, above: {above}")

# Collect all green objects
clicks = []
for n in green_objects:
    boundary = n['boundary']
    rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
    cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
    center_row = (min(rows) + max(rows)) // 2
    center_col = (min(cols) + max(cols)) // 2
    clicks.append({'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': center_row, 'col': center_col})

action(clicks)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
